groups.sentence: Instructors state in the course that they will not run student work through AI detection software.
AI detection tools are unreliable and produce false positives and false negatives.
Instructors do not use AI detection tools, and the university discourages relying on them.
Instructors use AI detection tools with caution.
AI detectors are biased against non-native English speakers and other groups of students.
Instructors rely on human judgment and other evidence rather than detection tools alone.
False positives risk false accusations, harm students, and erode trust.
Instructors do not treat AI detector results as definitive proof or the sole basis of misconduct.
Administrators do not use detection scores or results as evidence in academic misconduct cases.
AI detectors can be evaded through editing, rewording, or humanizing tools.
Instructors may use detector results as a guide, starting point, or supplementary tool, not a grading metric.
Administrators keep monitoring and reviewing AI detection tools over time.
The university does not license, approve, endorse, or provide an AI detection tool.
Instructors note other advice about detection tools, such as tool behavior, privacy, and teaching students instead.
The university has disabled, cancelled, or let expire its AI detection feature.
